research.title: The keystone experiment: image a single release event, both directions
research.summary: Put ultrafast shear-wave elastography and sensitive microvascular Doppler (or NIRS) over a palpated knot; apply calibrated constant pressure through a load-cell-instrumented probe; have a skilled releaser press a button at each felt release while respiration, HRV, and EMG are recorded. Sites localized in advance by two blinded examiners with the analysis volume predefined. Factorial controls: pressure with normal breathing, slow breathing without pressure, sham sites, and failed attempts. Add the stressor block: mental arithmetic under the imager, predicting local stiffening and perfusion drop during a purely cognitive event, then reversal on breath-assisted release. Preregistered prediction: stiffness step-drops and perfusion rises together, within seconds, time-locked to the exhale, exceeding all controls — with the latch-specific ordering that perfusion rises before stiffness falls. Falsification: felt releases without reproducible local transitions, or equal transitions at shams.
research.informationGain: Decides the case's central crux in one study (~$50–150K, one lab, one year): either direction is decisive, and a positive stressor block would demonstrate the full write–erase cycle in a single session.

research.title: The knot census: a natural-history atlas of human tension
research.summary: The dataset that has never existed: several hundred participants across the age span, standardized blinded palpation plus pressure algometry plus elastography and Doppler sampling at fixed bilateral anatomical sites. Report variance and spatial heterogeneity (lumpiness), not just means — every prior aging study discarded the heterogeneity as noise. Distinguish active from latent points, which separate on flow measures. Include the two discriminating populations: young children (if guarding is learned, they should be nearly clean) and long-term meditators against sedentary controls. Train imaging thresholds on one cohort and lock them before validation.
research.informationGain: Produces the two curves the field lacks (knot burden by age; distribution across the body), converts the ubiquity claim from anecdote to data, and supplies the localization protocol every other study needs.

research.title: The factorial intervention trial: separate the probe from the permission
research.summary: Randomize intensive rolling with breath work against rolling without breath instruction, breath work without rolling, and a stretching control over 8–12 weeks. Outcomes: knot counts from the census protocol, hip range of motion, elastography, HRV, and interoceptive awareness. The factorial design cleanly tests the two-key claim — that pressure and exhalation are jointly, not separately, sufficient — against the conventional prediction that generalized relaxation plus mechanical stimulus explains everything.
research.informationGain: The most clinically legible study in the program: it either validates a cheap, teachable release protocol or shows breath adds nothing local beyond relaxation — and buys credibility for the stranger tiers either way.

research.title: Demonstrate (or exclude) a smooth-muscle latch at a tender point
research.summary: The mechanism study the hypothesis cannot skip: in animal or ex-vivo preparations, create candidate tender-point-like regions (sustained low-level motor activity; controlled stress paradigms) and measure vessel radius, smooth-muscle calcium, myosin light-chain phosphorylation, perfusion, and tissue mechanics simultaneously. Make it a paired-caliber design rather than a single positive-or-negative arteriole test: take a feeding artery and successive arteriole orders from the same skeletal-muscle bed, cannulated and pressurized to physiological transmural pressure rather than held isometric, so the experiment reports whether latch capacity persists, weakens, or disappears as vessels get smaller — the boundary condition VASO-S001 has now audited in the published record, where latch behaviour was present in a parent artery and absent one branch order later. Include an explicit stimulus-withdrawal phase: economical force maintenance under continuing activation is a different finding from a state that holds after its input stops, and only the second is what a knot requires. Separately manipulate neural drive and vascular tone (sympathetic blockade, nitric-oxide pathway agents) and test whether releasing vascular tone precedes normalization of stiffness and nociception. In humans, add vasomotor endpoints to the keystone rig — the latch prediction is a timing signature: blood first, stiffness second. And run the small FDG-PET overlay testing the triple signature no conventional lesion carries: stiff on elastography, electrically active on EMG, metabolically cold.
research.informationGain: Turns "the mechanism is borrowed, not observed" into a direct test: finding latch-state smooth muscle at tender points would transform the case; excluding it would force the featured hypothesis back to conventional guarding accounts.

research.title: The decisive vasocomputation experiment: can vascular state carry a neural trace?
research.summary: From the critical report, the experiment that separates vascular modulation from vascular memory: in an animal preparation with optical access, repeatedly evoke a neural pattern while inducing a candidate vascular state; stop the input; after a delay, test whether the maintained vascular state biases neural responses back toward the trained pattern under identical stimulation — with oxygenation and metabolic variables clamped, so nonspecific ischemic suppression cannot masquerade as memory. Positive result: different induced vascular states produce reliably different later neural response distributions. Falsification: vascular manipulation affects neural gain only through instantaneous perfusion.
research.informationGain: The theory-deciding study: a positive result would establish a genuinely new biological memory mechanism; a clean negative would collapse strong vasocomputation to ordinary neurovascular physiology.

research.title: Preregistered anatomical coding of the contemplative knot maps
research.summary: The unglamorous scholarship the convergence argument needs: translate and annotate the rtsa mdud (channel-knot) literature and the granthi and ashi-point corpora with scholars fluent in both traditions and modern anatomy. Code traditional knot locations into a common coordinate system before inspecting modern maps, then test whether they align with vascular branch points, sympathetic chains, dorsal root ganglia, or dense-fascia geography better than chance — the blinded design that separates first-person cartography from post-hoc resemblance.
research.informationGain: Either elevates the traditional maps to admissible empirical documents or retires the convergence argument as pattern-matching — cheap, decisive for its claim, and publishable in either direction.

research.title: Where has the latch actually been demonstrated? An evidence map by vessel type and caliber
research.summary: The mechanism rung rested on an inferential step nothing in the ledger then checked: latch behaviour exists in vascular smooth muscle, therefore it can hold a skeletal-muscle microvessel shut. Build a preregistered evidence map of every eligible primary study — located through a frozen search strategy, citation chaining, and author-family searches — in which sustained force or constriction was measured alongside a contemporaneous readout of activation, cross-bridge cycling, or energetic cost. Record the vessel and its branch order, the luminal diameter and the pressure at which it was measured, the preparation (isometric ring versus cannulated pressurized vessel), temperature, the stimulus, whether the stimulus was withdrawn, and what the force did afterwards. Grade every record twice and independently: how directly it evidences the phenomenon, and how close its preparation is to the pressurized skeletal-muscle arteriole VASO-C020 needs. Models, reviews, and purified-protein reconstitutions are kept in distinct evidence classes rather than counted as vessel-level demonstrations. Executed as VASO-S001.
research.informationGain: Executed as VASO-S001, the map returned the extrapolation finding and the mixed finding together: the demonstration record is concentrated in large tonic conduit preparations, no energetic measurement exists in any arteriole, pressurized skeletal-muscle arterioles show maintained activation rather than an economical dephosphorylated hold, and the one paired comparison found latch behaviour in a parent artery but absent one branch order downstream — establishing C020 as an extrapolation across vessel type and caliber and fixing the boundary condition VASO-R004's paired-caliber design now targets. What it could not settle is whether knots are vascular; only whether the mechanism has ever been observed in the compartment the hypothesis needs it in — and, on the located record, it has not.
research.statusNote: Executed as study VASO-S001 (criteria frozen 2026-09-01; sixteen rows collected). Its table produced VASO-E019 (no energetic measurement exists in any arteriole; the economy argument rests on conduit arteries), VASO-E020 (pressurized skeletal-muscle arterioles show maintained or rising phosphorylation, not a latch signature) and VASO-E021 (latch behaviour present in the rabbit femoral artery and absent in its saphenous branch; never followed downstream). The map answered its own question — where the latch has been demonstrated — and fixed the boundary condition VASO-R004's paired-caliber design now targets; whether knots are vascular remains open under R001, R004 and R016.

research.title: Densification versus latch: does fascial hyaluronan densification account for a reversible, non-vascular release?
research.summary: The essay invokes the Stecco group's distinction between fascial densification (viscous hyaluronan between fascial sheets, reversible with pressure, movement, and warmth) and true scarring. If densification reverses on a timescale of seconds under sustained pressure, it is a state-not-structure mechanism that needs no vascular smooth muscle, competing directly with the latched-arteriole account. Desk route: retrieve the primary densification literature (Stecco and colleagues on hyaluronan viscosity, temperature dependence, and mechanical reversal), extract the measured or modelled timescale of viscosity change under load and warmth, and record whether any study reports reversal within the seconds-scale window the anchor phenomenon requires.
research.informationGain: If densification can reverse in seconds under pressure alone, VASO-C011 (state not structure) survives but the vascular attribution in VASO-C020 loses its claim to be the only fast mechanism, and the keystone experiment (VASO-R001) needs a discriminating prediction — perfusion change with the stiffness drop (vascular) versus stiffness drop without perfusion change (densification). If densification reversal is minutes-to-hours, the vascular account remains the only candidate for a seconds-scale objective release.

research.title: Locate the phentolamine trigger-point study: does sympathetic blockade quiet the nidus?
research.summary: The essay states that later work from the Hubbard–Gevirtz lineage infused trigger-point sites with phentolamine, an alpha-adrenergic antagonist, and substantially quieted the spontaneous EMG activity. The report's works list did not carry this item and no candidate was resolved. Desk route: search the needle-EMG trigger-point literature of the 1990s (Hubbard, Gevirtz, McNulty, Banks and co-authors; journals of pain, psychophysiology, and physical medicine) for a sympathetic-blockade study, retrieve the primary paper, and record the design, n, control condition, and effect. A sympathetic-dependence result would be the strongest existing link between the electrical nidus and autonomic maintenance.
research.informationGain: A retrieved primary study showing phentolamine quiets trigger-point EMG would support autonomic maintenance of the nidus (bearing on VASO-C002/C003) and supply the pharmacological arm of VASO-R004, though it would not by itself distinguish vascular smooth-muscle latching from sympathetically driven intrafusal or endplate activity. Failure to locate any such study would show the essay's autonomic-maintenance argument rests on stress-induction alone.

research.title: Retrieve the fibromyalgia-era community tender-point-count surveys as a proto-census
research.summary: The essay reports, without citation, that population-based studies using the 18-site fibromyalgia tender-point exam found tender points nearly universal (medians 6 in women, 3 in men) and counts tracking distress and sleep rather than tissue damage. If a primary paper exists — the candidates are the 1990s population surveys of tender-point counts in general-population samples (e.g., the UK and Wichita community studies) — it is the only instrumented prevalence data behind VASO-C001 and the only existing curve of tender-point burden against sex, age, and distress. Desk task: locate the primary papers, retrieve the count distributions, and record whether the exam sites and pressure protocol map onto what the case calls a 'knot'.
research.informationGain: Would give VASO-C001 its first population-level, examiner-administered evidence record (currently supported only by proponent testimony and qualified by the reliability critique), would reveal whether tender-point counts already correlate with age, and would tell VASO-R002 what the census must add beyond what rheumatology already measured and abandoned.

research.title: Needle EMG at a trigger point versus a matched endplate-zone control site under mental arithmetic
research.summary: Simons 2002 shows endplate noise occurs at non-tender endplate-zone sites, so the silent control sites in Hubbard–Berkoff 1993 and McNulty 1994 may simply have been off the endplate zone. Repeat the McNulty stressor paradigm with the endplate zone located electrically first, placing the control needle in a non-tender endplate-zone site of the same muscle and recording both sites during baseline, serial subtraction, and slow-exhalation recovery. Preregister the contrast: does the stressor raise activity selectively at the trigger point, or at any endplate-zone site?
research.informationGain: Selective rise at the trigger point with a quiet matched endplate-zone control would restore the 'addressable nidus' reading VASO-C003 rests on; a comparable rise at the control would relocate the phenomenon to stress-sensitive endplates generally and remove the localization argument for a discrete maintained element.

research.title: Open the located-but-unretrieved primaries behind this pass (Banks 1998, Hubbard 1996, Chen 1998, Zhang 2009, Ge 2011)
research.summary: The report located, but the pipeline could not retrieve, five papers each of which would anchor a record the ledger lacks (the sixth the report located, Landfald, Podgórski & Olewnik 2025, was retrieved and entered on 2026-09-20 as SRC-LANDFALD-2025): Banks et al. 1998 (autogenic relaxation lowering trigger-point needle EMG, same lineage as VASO-E002); Hubbard 1996 and Chen et al. 1998 (alpha-blockade quieting the nidus in humans and rabbits, VASO-R009); Zhang et al. 2009 (attenuated skin blood-flow response at latent points); Ge et al. 2011 (open-access review recording the curare-vs-botulinum conflict on whether the nidus is cholinergic). Routes: PMC or publisher PDFs where open access (Ge), PubMed abstract pages with cookies enabled (Chen, Zhang, Simons full text), a library or interlibrary copy for the Haworth-journal items (Banks, Hubbard).
research.informationGain: Would convert four blocked observations into anchored records: bidirectional autonomic modulation of the nidus (Banks), the phentolamine result VASO-R009 asks for (Hubbard, Chen), a measured autonomic-vascular abnormality at a latent point (Zhang), and the cholinergic-generator conflict (Ge). The imaged stiffness reversal under pressure alone that this item once waited for is now in the ledger from Landfald 2025 (VASO-E067 and its siblings), as context: the protocol recorded no breathing and its course ran to minutes, so it bears on 'state, not scar' only by inference.

research.title: FDG-PET overlaid on elastography at palpated knots: is the stiff, electrically active spot metabolically cold?
research.summary: Small overlay study: palpate and mark knots under blinded examiners, confirm stiffness by shear-wave elastography and spontaneous activity by needle EMG at a subset, then acquire FDG-PET and compare uptake at knot sites with matched non-tender muscle. The latch account predicts uptake at or below surrounding muscle; an energy-crisis (maximally contracting fibers) or inflammatory account predicts elevated uptake. Radiation limits this to a single small study, not a census.
research.informationGain: Cold knots would be the first finding that does not fit conventional lesion taxonomies and would specifically favour a low-energy holding state over active contraction or inflammation; hot knots would fit the energy-crisis or inflammatory accounts and remove the essay's distinctive metabolic prediction. Either result moves VASO-C020 in a way no imaging of stiffness or flow can.

research.title: Retrieve the primaries behind the newly catalogued affective and adverse-effect claims (Britton; Leknes & Tracey; Moseley/Flor)
research.summary: Desk retrieval: the peer-reviewed meditation adverse-effects study from Britton's Brown program (for VASO-C133), Leknes & Tracey's review of the shared neurobiology of pain and pleasure (for VASO-C128/C130's pain-offset reading), and a primary Moseley or Flor paper on somatosensory cortical reorganization in chronic pain (for VASO-C106). Each is named only in the essay; nothing can be anchored to them until their text is read.
research.informationGain: Replaces essay-only anchors with primary sources for five claims, and tells the case whether the affective phenomenology of release (bliss, immobility, destabilization) has any instrumented literature behind it or rests wholly on testimony.

research.title: Map the staples: blinded coincidence of palpated tender points with pencil-Doppler perforators against chance
research.summary: One blinded examiner marks tender points on a region of scalp, neck, back or hip; a second blinded operator maps cutaneous perforators on the same region by continuous-wave pencil Doppler at fixed light pressure; a third computes spatial coincidence against a chance baseline from randomized point sets. Settles whether ordinary knots sit on perforators (VASO-C101) and whether the most tender sit on the largest trunks; a null returns the vascular hypothesis to the intramuscular compartment or dissolves it.
research.informationGain: A cheap, afternoon-scale test that either licenses or kills the perforator alternative before any imaging is bought; a positive coincidence above chance would be the first objective anatomical identity for a palpated knot.

research.title: Film a star: laser speckle over a superficial knot with exhale, inhale-hold, sham-site and CO2 controls
research.summary: Laser speckle contrast imaging over the occiput or upper trapezius during breath-assisted release; mark a knot and a sham site, record respiration, end-tidal CO2, surface EMG and a button press at each felt release; apply calibrated pressure on exhale and, in matched trials, during an inhale-and-hold. Preregistered predictions: local perfusion flash time-locked to exhale and button, absent at sham and under inhale-hold (perforator account); versus global changes tracking CO2 (hyperventilation account).
research.informationGain: Directly discriminates the perforator, hyperventilation and no-local-event accounts of the felt release at the surface, where no depth problem exists, and tests the blood-first ordering with a non-contact method.

research.title: Free a collar without breath: ultrasound-guided saline hydrodissection at a mapped perforator under a tender point
research.summary: In a clinic already performing nerve hydrodissection, place a few milliliters of saline around a Doppler-mapped perforator at its fascial ring beneath a blinded-examiner tender point, with no breath instruction and no manual pressure; record tenderness (algometry), the felt star, and elastography before and after; sham injection adjacent to the bundle as control.
research.informationGain: The cleanest single test of the collared-perforator identification: release without breath refutes the two-key necessity (VASO-C039) and supports VASO-C101; no effect leaves the knot with motor guarding or another account.

research.title: The knot-free endpoint as a natural experiment, with a sensory exam to exclude a damaged finder
research.summary: Recruit practitioners who report having completed the release process; blinded examiner, standardized sites, pressure algometry, light-touch and pinprick sensory exam, Doppler perforator map, elastography, against age-matched controls. A blinded finding of no tender points in a middle-aged adult with normal sensation and normally perfused perforators supports the perforator account; reduced sensation with constricted perforators supports the hypoesthesia confound.
research.informationGain: Cheap and decisive for the endpoint prediction, and it cannot be gamed by expectation because the sensory exam separates 'no knots' from 'no finder'.

research.title: Open the primaries behind the second essay's audit (Heine 1988; Langevin & Yandow 2002; Dorsher 2009; Segal & Duling 1986; Hong & Simons 1993; Taylor & Palmer 1987; Lindahl 2017; Sikdar 2009; Moraska 2013; Cagnie 2012; Fede 2022)
research.summary: Desk retrieval of the eleven published works the essay restates as support, so that the essay's remaining claims (C128–C130, C136–C143) can be anchored to primaries and the essay-derived evidence records re-weighed; check Maurer et al. 2019 as the contrary dissection.
research.informationGain: Every one of these claims currently rests on an AI-generated essay's restatement; retrieval converts them to primary-anchored observations or exposes misreadings.

research.title: Repeat the runners' compression protocol with breathing recorded and randomised: free breathing, slow exhale, inhale-and-hold
research.summary: Take the now-verified single-session ischemic-compression protocol (30-s thumb compressions with 10-s rests, up to three rounds, palpation plus B-mode and strain or shear-wave elastography before, after each round and at 24 h) and add the one factor it left uncontrolled: breath. Record respiration continuously (inductance belt and end-tidal CO2) and randomise each trigger point within a participant to one of three conditions during compression — free breathing, instructed slow exhalation, or pressure applied only during an inhale-and-hold — with sham compression at a matched non-tender site as a fourth arm and a no-treatment point followed at the same time points. Measure, per point, whether the stiff focus is undetectable after the session and at 24 h, its stiffness ratio and cross-sectional area, and the pain score. Decision rule: if the elimination rate under inhale-and-hold is no lower than under free breathing, the breath is not a necessary key and the two-key claim fails; if inhale-and-hold blocks elimination while slow exhalation matches or exceeds free breathing, the breath-gating the perforator account predicts is real; if all three active arms exceed sham and no-treatment equally, pressure alone suffices and the felt release is a correlate. Archive cine loops and, where available, add power Doppler over the same region so the order of perfusion and stiffness change can be read.
research.informationGain: The one pressure-only protocol the ledger has read in full (Landfald 2025) applied its compressions with breathing uninstructed and unrecorded, over up to three thirty-second rounds — a course of minutes, not a release of seconds — and its record (VASO-E067) is context for the two-key claim, not evidence against it: it establishes what the method omitted, not what breath did or did not do. One session per participant with the breath factor randomised separates the three readings — breath necessary, breath gating, breath irrelevant — and, with the sham and no-treatment arms, separates the compression effect from expectation and regression. A positive inhale-hold block would be the first evidence for breath-gated release in any tissue; a null would return the exhale to the status of a felt correlate and move the case's anchor observation onto pressure alone.

images.alt: Hand-tinted anatomical-plate engraving in madder red and oxblood: a skeleton beside a tightly knotted vessel that connects by a slender tube to a brain, with two smooth-muscle spindles laid below.
images.credit: AI-generated editorial artwork, Aletheia house style
images.prompt: Hand-tinted 19th-century scientific expedition lithograph, chromolithograph plate from a vintage natural-history atlas. An allegorical emblem for a case titled "State, Not Scar?" in the domain of Musculoskeletal medicine · Autonomic physiology · Contemplative science: a symbolic, typological composition suggesting the question — Are muscle knots maintained vascular-autonomic states — latched smooth muscle — rather than damaged tissue, and does vascular tension participate in the mind? — without depicting any real site, artifact, or dataset as documentation. Fine copperplate cross-hatching and stipple engraving beneath soft, translucent hand-applied watercolor washes. Full color in subdued antique mineral pigments — madder red and oxblood on the vessel-like forms, faded rose flesh tones, ivory bone, a faint sage undertone — over warm-black ink linework on aged warm cream paper (#f6f1e8). Colors muted and slightly faded as if printed in 1870; never saturated modern digital color, no gradients, no glow. Darwin-era natural-history journal plate aesthetic, generous plain paper margins, quiet composition. Absolutely no text, no labels, no captions, no border frame lines. Unmistakably a hand-tinted engraving — stylized editorial artwork, not photorealistic, no photograph.
